questions.question: Ajaz accelerates at 0.8 m s^-2 from rest up to 4 m s^-1, then keeps this speed. Beth accelerates at 1 m s^-2 for T s from rest, then keeps a constant speed. They start together and finish a 100 m race at the same time. Sketch both speed-time graphs on the same axes until they cross the finish line.
questions.answer: Ajaz: straight line (0,0) to (5,4), then level at 4 m s^-1 to t = 27.5 s. Beth: straight line (0,0) to (3.92,3.92), then level at 3.92 m s^-1 to t = 27.5 s.
steps: Ajaz: time to reach 4 m s^-1 is 4/0.8 = 5 s, so the line runs from (0,0) to (5,4), then level.
Beth: speed at time t is t for 0 <= t <= T, so the line runs from (0,0) to (T,T), with T from part (c).
After T, Beth's graph is level at speed T until both finish at 27.5 s (from part (b)).
Both graphs end at the same time, 27.5 s, so the areas under them are both 100 m.

questions.question: Ajaz accelerates at 0.8 m s^-2 up to 4 m s^-1 and then keeps this speed until he crosses the finish line of a 100 m race. Find the time taken by Ajaz to complete the race.
steps: Accelerating phase: t1 = 4/0.8 = 5 s, distance = (1/2)(0.8)(5^2) = 10 m.
Constant speed phase: distance remaining = 100 - 10 = 90 m.
Total time = 5 + 22.5 = 27.5 s.

questions.question: Beth accelerates at 1 m s^-2 for T s from rest, then moves at constant speed until she crosses the 100 m finish line at the same time as Ajaz. Find the value of T.
steps: Beth's speed at the end of the acceleration is T m s^-1, and she covers 0.5T^2 m in this phase.
Remaining distance 100 - 0.5T^2 is covered at constant speed T, taking (100 - 0.5T^2)/T s.
Multiply by 2T: T^2 - 55T + 200 = 0.
T = (55 - sqrt(2225))/2 = 3.92 s (3 s.f.), taking the root with 0.5T^2 < 100.

questions.question: Find the difference in the speeds of Ajaz and Beth as they cross the finish line.
steps: Ajaz's speed at the finish is 4 m s^-1.
Beth's speed at the finish is T = 3.915 m s^-1 (from part (c)).

questions.question: A car starts from rest and accelerates uniformly for 30 s until it reaches speed V m s^-1, then travels at constant speed V until time t = T. Show that the distance travelled between t = 0 and t = T is V(T - 15) metres.
steps: Distance = area under the speed-time graph.
Accelerating phase is a triangle: (1/2) x 30 x V = 15V.
Constant speed phase lasts T - 30 s: V(T - 30).
Total = 15V + VT - 30V = V(T - 15) (shown).

questions.question: A motorbike starts from rest at t = 10 s and accelerates uniformly for 40 s with the same acceleration as the car. It then travels at constant speed for 10 s, then decelerates uniformly until it reaches speed V at time T. Sketch its speed-time graph on Figure 2.
questions.answer: Straight line (10,0) to (50, 4V/3), level to (60, 4V/3), then straight line down to (T, V).
steps: Acceleration of the car is a = V/30, so the motorbike reaches 40a = 4V/3 after 40 s.
Accelerating phase: straight line from (10,0) to (50, 4V/3).
Constant speed phase: level at 4V/3 from t = 50 to t = 60.
Deceleration phase: straight line from (60, 4V/3) down to (T, V).

questions.question: The motorbike has the same acceleration as the car and accelerates uniformly from rest at t = 10 s for 40 s. Show that its constant speed is 4V/3 m s^-1.
steps: Car acceleration: a = V/30 (V gained in 30 s).
Motorbike accelerates for 40 s with the same acceleration: speed = 40 x V/30.
Speed = 4V/3 m s^-1 (shown).

questions.question: At time t = T the car and motorbike have travelled the same distance. The motorbike starts at t = 10 s, accelerates for 40 s, moves at constant speed for 10 s, then decelerates uniformly to speed V at time T. Find T.
steps: Car distance by time T: V(T - 15).
Motorbike distance: accelerating (1/2)(40)(4V/3) = 80V/3; constant speed 10 x 4V/3 = 40V/3; total so far 40V.
Deceleration phase from 60 s to T: speeds 4V/3 to V, distance (7V/6)(T - 60).
Equal distances: V(T - 15) = 40V + (7V/6)(T - 60).
Divide by V: T - 15 = 40 + 7T/6 - 70, so T/6 = 15 and T = 90 s.

questions.question: A train starts from rest at station A and accelerates uniformly for T s to 20 m s^-1. It then travels at 20 m s^-1 for 3 minutes, then decelerates uniformly to rest at station B. The acceleration magnitude is twice the deceleration magnitude. Sketch the speed-time graph from A to B.
questions.answer: Straight line (0,0) to (T,20), level to (T+180, 20), straight line down to (3T+180, 0), with T = 40 s.
steps: Acceleration = 20/T; deceleration = 10/T, so the deceleration lasts 20/(10/T) = 2T s.
Graph: straight line from (0,0) to (T,20).
Level at 20 m s^-1 for 180 s, from T to T + 180.
Straight line down from (T + 180, 20) to (3T + 180, 0).

questions.question: Stations A and B are 4.8 km apart. The train accelerates from rest to 20 m s^-1 in T s, travels at 20 m s^-1 for 3 minutes, then decelerates uniformly to rest at B, with the deceleration half the acceleration. Find the value of T.
steps: Distance = area under speed-time graph; AB = 4800 m.
Accelerating triangle: (1/2)(T)(20) = 10T.
Constant speed: 20 x 180 = 3600 m.
Decelerating triangle: (1/2)(2T)(20) = 20T.

questions.question: Find the acceleration of the train during the first T seconds of its motion, given T = 40 s and the train reaches 20 m s^-1.
steps: Acceleration = change in speed / time = (20 - 0)/T.

questions.question: Tram A starts from rest at t = 0 with acceleration 2 m s^-2 for 5 s, then moves at constant speed. Tram B starts from rest at t = 20 s with acceleration 3 m s^-2 for 4 s, then moves at constant speed, in the same direction. Sketch both speed-time graphs on the same axes until tram B overtakes tram A.
questions.answer: Tram A: (0,0) to (5,10), level at 10 m s^-1. Tram B: (20,0) to (24,12), level at 12 m s^-1. B overtakes A at t = 119.5 s.
steps: Tram A: straight line from (0,0) to (5,10), then level at 10 m s^-1.
Tram B: straight line from (20,0) to (24,12), then level at 12 m s^-1.
Overtaking occurs when the areas under the graphs are equal; the sketch runs until overtaking at t = 119.5 s (part (c)).

questions.question: At the instant when the two trams are moving with the same speed, tram A is d m in front of tram B. Find d.
steps: Tram A is at speed 10 m s^-1 from t = 5 s onwards; tram B is at speed 3(t - 20) for 20 <= t <= 24.
Equal speeds: 3(t - 20) = 10, so t = 70/3 s (before B reaches 12 m s^-1).
Position of A at t = 70/3: 10t - 25 = 625/3 m (A moves 25 m in first 5 s, then 10 m/s).

questions.question: Find the distance of the trams from the depot at the instant when tram B overtakes tram A.
steps: Tram A after 5 s: displacement = 25 + 10(t - 5) = 10t - 25 m for t >= 5.
Tram B after 24 s: displacement = 24 + 12(t - 24) = 12t - 264 m for t >= 24.
Overtaking when 10t - 25 = 12t - 264, so t = 119.5 s.

questions.question: Cars A and B are at rest at points P and Q on parallel tracks. A starts to move at t = 0 with constant acceleration a m s^-2 for 3.5 s, reaching 14 m s^-1, then moves at constant speed 14 m s^-1. Find the value of a.
steps: Use v = u + at with u = 0, v = 14, t = 3.5.

questions.question: Car B starts from Q at t = 0 with constant acceleration 3 m s^-2 in the same direction as A. At t = T, B overtakes A, which is then moving at constant speed. Sketch the speed-time graphs of A and B for 0 <= t <= T on the same axes.
questions.answer: A: straight line (0,0) to (3.5,14), then level at 14 to t = 7. B: straight line from (0,0) to (7,21), with T = 7 s from part (c).
steps: A: speed rises linearly from 0 to 14 at t = 3.5 s, then stays level at 14 m s^-1.
B: speed rises linearly from (0,0) with gradient 3 m s^-2.
Both graphs run until t = T = 7 s (from part (c)); B reaches 21 m s^-1 there.
The area under each graph gives the distance travelled, used in parts (c) and (d).

questions.question: Car A accelerates at 4 m s^-2 for 3.5 s to 14 m s^-1, then moves at constant speed. Car B starts from rest at Q at t = 0 with constant acceleration 3 m s^-2, both in the same direction. B overtakes A at t = T. Find T.
steps: Car A displacement: accelerating phase 0.5 x 4 x 3.5^2 = 24.5 m; then 14(T - 3.5).
Car B displacement: 0.5 x 3 x T^2 = 1.5T^2.

questions.question: Find the distance of car B from the point Q when B overtakes A at T = 7 s, where B has acceleration 3 m s^-2 from rest at Q.
steps: B starts at Q from rest with a = 3 m s^-2.
Distance = 0.5 x 3 x 7^2 = 73.5 m.

questions.question: On a new diagram, sketch the acceleration-time graphs for car A and car B for 0 <= t <= T, with T = 7 s. A has acceleration 4 m s^-2 for 3.5 s then 0. B has constant acceleration 3 m s^-2.
questions.answer: A: 4 m s^-2 from t = 0 to 3.5, then 0 from 3.5 to 7. B: constant 3 m s^-2 from t = 0 to 7.
steps: A: horizontal line at 4 m s^-2 from t = 0 to t = 3.5 s.
A: horizontal line at 0 from t = 3.5 s to t = 7 s (constant speed).
B: horizontal line at 3 m s^-2 from t = 0 to t = 7 s.

questions.question: A ball is projected vertically upwards at t = 0 from A, which is 24.5 m above the ground. It first comes to instantaneous rest at B where AB = 19.6 m, then first hits the ground at t = T. It is modelled as a particle under gravity. Find T.
steps: Upwards positive, A at origin. At B (height 19.6 m), v = 0: 0 = u^2 - 2(9.8)(19.6), so u = 19.6 m s^-1.
Time to reach B: 0 = 19.6 - 9.8t, so t = 2 s.
Ground is 24.5 m below A: -24.5 = 19.6T - 4.9T^2.
T = 5 s.

questions.question: Sketch a speed-time graph for the ball from t = 0 to t = T, where T = 5 s, with no further calculations needed.
questions.answer: Speed-time graph: straight line from (0, 19.6) down to (2, 0), then straight line up to (5, 29.4).
steps: Speed falls linearly at 9.8 m s^-2 from 19.6 m s^-1 at t = 0 to 0 at t = 2 s (top point B).
Speed then rises linearly at 9.8 m s^-2 from 0 at t = 2 s.
At t = 5 s the speed is 9.8 x 3 = 29.4 m s^-1, the ground speed.

questions.question: A ball is projected vertically upwards with speed 29.4 m s^-1 from A, which is 19.6 m above horizontal ground. It does not rebound. Find the distance travelled by the ball while its speed is less than 14.7 m s^-1.
steps: Maximum height above A: 29.4^2/(2 x 9.8) = 44.1 m.
Speed is less than 14.7 m s^-1 only in the top part of the motion, where the ball is 14.7^2/(2 x 9.8) = 11.025 m below its highest point.
On the way up, this is from 44.1 - 11.025 to 44.1, a distance of 11.025 m.
On the way down the same distance is travelled, so total = 2 x 11.025 = 22.05 m.

questions.question: Find the time for which the ball is moving with a speed of more than 29.4 m s^-1, given it is projected at 29.4 m s^-1 from A, 19.6 m above horizontal ground.
steps: Taking upwards as positive, speed exceeds 29.4 m s^-1 only when the ball is falling faster than it was at A.
It is at A with speed 29.4 m s^-1 on the way down at t = 6 s (since it rises for 3 s).
Ground is 19.6 m below A: -19.6 = 29.4t - 4.9t^2, so t^2 - 6t - 4 = 0.
t = 3 + sqrt(13) = 6.61 s when it hits the ground.
Time with speed greater than 29.4 m s^-1 = (3 + sqrt(13)) - 6 = sqrt(13) - 3 = 0.606 s.

questions.question: Sketch a speed-time graph for the ball from projection at A until it hits the ground, showing clearly where the graph meets the axes. The ball is projected at 29.4 m s^-1 from 19.6 m above ground.
questions.answer: V-shaped graph from (0, 29.4) down to (3, 0), then up to (3 + sqrt(13), 35.3); meets the speed axis at 29.4 and the time axis at t = 3 s.
steps: At t = 0 the speed is 29.4 m s^-1 (meets the speed axis there).
Speed falls linearly at 9.8 m s^-2 to 0 at t = 3 s (the top, meets the time axis).
Speed then rises linearly at 9.8 m s^-2 from 0 at t = 3 s, reaching 29.4 m s^-1 at t = 6 s and 35.3 m s^-1 at ground impact (t = 6.61 s).

questions.question: A car passes A with speed 8 m s^-1 at t = 0 and travels along a road to B. Figure 2 is an acceleration-time graph: acceleration -0.5 m s^-2 for 0 <= t < 4, 0 for 4 <= t < 10, and 1.2 m s^-2 for 10 <= t <= 20. Show that the speed at B (t = 20 s) is v = 18 m s^-1.
steps: Change in velocity = area under the acceleration-time graph.
Area for 0 to 4 s: -0.5 x 4 = -2; for 4 to 10 s: 0; for 10 to 20 s: 1.2 x 10 = 12.
Total change = -2 + 0 + 12 = 10 m s^-1.

questions.question: Sketch a speed-time graph for the car from A to B, using the acceleration-time graph in Figure 2 and the speeds 8 m s^-1 at A and 18 m s^-1 at B.
questions.answer: Straight line (0,8) to (4,6), level at 6 to t = 10, then straight line up to (20,18).
steps: 0 to 4 s: acceleration -0.5, so speed falls by 2 to 6 m s^-1 (line from (0,8) to (4,6)).
4 to 10 s: acceleration 0, so speed stays at 6 m s^-1 (level line).
10 to 20 s: acceleration 1.2, so speed rises by 12 to 18 m s^-1 (line from (10,6) to (20,18)).

questions.question: Using the speed-time graph for the car from A (8 m s^-1) to B (18 m s^-1) over 20 s, find the distance AB.
steps: Interval 0 to 4 s: trapezium with speeds 8 and 6: (8 + 6)/2 x 4 = 28 m.
Interval 4 to 10 s: speed 6 m s^-1: 6 x 6 = 36 m.
Interval 10 to 20 s: trapezium with speeds 6 and 18: (6 + 18)/2 x 10 = 120 m.
